quote: Suppose that Vj has the MoD with parameter δj for j = 1, 2. Let Hj(v; δj) be the CDF and hj(v; δj) be the PDF of Vj. Then V1 is said to be stochastically smaller than V2 with respect to likelihood ratio order (say V1 ≤lr V2), if h1(v;δ1)/h2(v;δ2) is a decreasing function ∀ v values. ... Then, for δ2 < δ1, we obtain d/dv log[h1(v;δ1)/h2(v;δ2)] < 0 ∀v ≥ 0. So, d/dv log[h1(v;δ1)/h2(v;δ2)] is decreasing in v and consequently V1 ≤lr V2. Furthermore, V1 is said to be smaller than V2 in other different orderings as (SO, represented as V1 ≤so V2), (hazard rate order; represented by V1 ≤hr V2), and (reversed hazard rate order; represented by V1 ≤rhr V2) (see Shaked and Shanthikumar [39]).
family: Monsef distribution (MoD): pdf h(v;δ) ∝ δ^3 (v+1)^2 e^{−δv} / [δ(δ+2)+2] type
compared: V1 ~ MoD(δ1) vs V2 ~ MoD(δ2) with δ2 < δ1

conclusion.direction: V1 ≤_lr V2; consequently V1 ≤_st V2 (so), V1 ≤_hr V2, V1 ≤_rhr V2
